newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Crude Outlook - soft market ahead of Easter.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Crude Outlook - soft market ahead of Easter.

text.p: U.S. crude prices are likely to hover in a soft range this week, reflecting a continued perception of abundant physical supplies ahead of the Easter holidays beginning on Friday, industry analysts and traders said on Monday.

Plentiful domestic and foreign supplies are weighing down futures prices, a trend that's unlikely to change course until gasoline demand gets into full swing in late April or early May, analysts said.

"I expect a stop-and-go pattern as the futures market tries to get into sync with the physical market," said William Brown, president of W.H. Brown and Co in New York. "There will be a pull-and-tug until you get both the futures and physicals lined up."

Tom Bentz of ING Derivatives in New York suggested prices would remain rangebound to weaker. "Right now, everything looks like it's pointing to lower numbers," he said. "There's plenty of crude around...that still seems to be the perception."
April cash crude differentials weakened as activity winds down ahead of Tuesday's pipeline scheduling.

A seemingly relentless influx of crudes from the North Sea, West Africa and Latin America continued to pressure domestic sweet grades. Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James traded at a discount of 10 cents to West Texas Intermediate/Cushing, five to 10 cents lower than last deals for April.
May business isn't expected to get off to a start until next week.
"I think it'll be a slow week," said broker John Troland with Belmont Crude in Houston. "A lot of people got done on Friday."
The New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) and London's International Petroleum Exchange are closed on March 28 to observe Good Friday. London is also closed on Monday, the day after Easter.
